subject: Day 63: coax the first laugh
bodyText:
Today's focus
Week 10 opens, and many infants produce their first true laugh in the 10-14 week range. Social reciprocity is sharpening fast, so this week is about playing for that laugh and answering every chuckle.

Action items
- Play exaggerated peek-a-boo and gentle tickle games during his most alert window and watch for the first laugh, which commonly emerges between 10 and 14 weeks; some infants wait until 14-16 weeks, which is still normal. AAP Bright Futures: https://www.aap.org/en/practice-management/bright-futures/bright-futures-tools-and-resources/
- Begin tracking sleep windows this week, logging last wake, time he fell asleep, and nap length; the pattern stabilizes enough by 12-14 weeks to anchor a loose schedule before the 4-month regression. AAP infant sleep: https://www.healthychildren.org/English/ages-stages/baby/sleep/Pages/default.aspx
- Book a 100-day or 3-month photo session now if you want one, since week 12-14 is the window and the better photographers are scheduling weeks out.

Watch-fors
- [low concern] Profuse drooling and hand-sucking, which reflect salivary-gland maturation rather than teething; first teeth typically arrive at 6-10 months.
- [monitor] Persistent head asymmetry or flattening on one side; reposition during sleep and held time and flag at the next visit if it does not respond.
- [call within 24h] Decreased feeding lasting more than 24 hours, or any new color change during feeds.
- [call now] Rectal temperature of 100.4F (38.0C) or higher under 90 days, an apnea pause, or seizure-like activity needs a call now, and 911 for blue lips.

Enrichment opportunities
- Play exaggerated peek-a-boo and light tummy raspberries face-to-face to elicit early laughs, repeating the gag that lands; the surprise-and-resolution structure is what tips a coo into a chuckle. AAP Bright Futures: https://www.aap.org/en/practice-management/bright-futures/bright-futures-tools-and-resources/
- Cheer and answer every chuckle to extend the back-and-forth, treating each sound as a turn and pausing for his next one; the reciprocity is what builds later language. Romeo et al. 2018: https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/29442613/
- Add one new book this week alongside the repeats at roughly a 3:1 repeat-to-novel ratio, which balances prosodic familiarity against lexical novelty. AAP early literacy: https://www.aap.org/en/patient-care/early-childhood/early-literacy/

Upcoming
- Day 70-76: confirm caregivers and grandparents are current on Tdap before more contact, since pertussis is the contact-borne illness most dangerous to infants.
- Day 84-91: sleep-consolidation window opens near three months; start a consistent sleep-wake routine.
- Day 112-126: 4-month well visit, with RV #2, DTaP #2, Hib #2, PCV #2, and IPV #2.

Developmental milestone check-in
Tap any link to mark it complete. View or change others at https://www.noahhshaw.com/baby/milestones

- Smiles on his own to get your attention
  AAP window: day 60-120
  What to look for: Initiates the smile rather than responding to yours — emerging social agency.
  Source: https://www.cdc.gov/act-early/milestones/4-months.html
  Mark complete: https://www.noahhshaw.com/baby/milestones/smiles-to-get-attention/complete

- Chuckles (not yet a full laugh)
  AAP window: day 60-120
  What to look for: Throaty soft laugh sounds. Precedes the full belly laugh by a few weeks.
  Source: https://www.cdc.gov/act-early/milestones/4-months.html
  Mark complete: https://www.noahhshaw.com/baby/milestones/chuckles/complete

- Turns head toward the sound of your voice
  AAP window: day 60-120
  What to look for: Localizes sound source. Worth raising with the pediatrician if absent at the 4-month visit.
  Source: https://www.cdc.gov/act-early/milestones/4-months.html
  Mark complete: https://www.noahhshaw.com/baby/milestones/turns-head-toward-sound/complete

- Makes sounds back when you talk to him
  AAP window: day 60-120
  What to look for: Conversational turn-taking. Foundation for later vocabulary growth.
  Source: https://www.cdc.gov/act-early/milestones/4-months.html
  Mark complete: https://www.noahhshaw.com/baby/milestones/makes-sounds-back/complete

- Opens mouth when she sees the breast or bottle
  AAP window: day 60-120
  What to look for: Anticipatory recognition — feeding is now associated with the sight, not just the sensation.
  Source: https://www.cdc.gov/act-early/milestones/4-months.html
  Mark complete: https://www.noahhshaw.com/baby/milestones/opens-mouth-for-breast/complete
